questions.question: What is antimony, and which forms matter?
questions.answer: Antimony (Sb) is a metalloid. Trivalent antimony, including antimony trioxide and antimony potassium tartrate, is not the same hazard as pentavalent antimony. IARC Monograph Volume 131, announced on 5 May 2023, classifies trivalent antimony as Group 2A (probably carcinogenic to humans) and pentavalent antimony as Group 3 (not classifiable). Antimony trioxide was Group 2B in the 1989 evaluation. The 2023 classification is of the trivalent class, which includes antimony trioxide, rather than a separate line that names only the oxide.

questions.question: How do people come into contact with antimony?
questions.answer: IARC lists uses in flame retardants, plastics, brake pads, glass, ceramics, and lead alloys. WHO's drinking-water fact sheet treats plumbing and fittings as the common drinking-water source and states that drinking-water concentrations appear to be below 5 µg/L. [[sources/ungureanu2022-bottled-water-toxic-elements|Ungureanu and colleagues 2022]] measured bottled-water antimony in Romania from below 0.07 µg/L to a printed maximum of 0.64 ± 6.85 µg/L. [[sources/stone2021-wa-metals-childrens-consumer-products|Washington Ecology]] measured tens of ppm of antimony in screened baby-wipe, bib, and clothing components. Those product figures are a prioritized screen, not a random market mean. No dermal absorption percent for wipe or textile contact is stated on this page.

questions.question: What oral reference values and water limits are on this page?
questions.answer: WHO's tolerable daily intake is 6 µg/kg body weight, from a NOAEL of 6.0 mg/kg/day in a 90-day rat study of potassium antimony tartrate and an uncertainty factor of 1000. The drinking-water guideline is 0.02 mg/L. ATSDR's 2019 intermediate oral minimal risk level is 0.0006 mg Sb/kg/day, from a much lower NOAEL (0.06 mg Sb/kg/day) on the same study, and there is no chronic oral minimal risk level. The U.S. EPA maximum contaminant level is 0.006 mg/L. These values are not averaged. The EPA IRIS oral reference dose was not opened for this revision, so it is not stated.

questions.question: Do toy, food-contact, and cosmetic limits mean the same thing?
questions.answer: No. EU 10/2011 sets a specific migration limit of 0.04 mg/kg into food from plastic. EN 71-3 sets soluble toy migration at 45, 11.3, and 560 mg/kg of toy material for Categories I, II, and III. Health Canada cosmetic guidance is 5 ppm in a finished cosmetic and is guidance, not a wipe regulation. EU cosmetics law prohibits antimony and its compounds as ingredients (Annex II, entry 40) and sets no trace ppm in Article 17. A drinking-water limit cannot be copied onto a textile or a wipe. The corpus OEKO-TEX record used here is a wastewater limit of 100 µg/L, not an extractable limit in a finished article.

questions.question: What is known about antimony and microbes?
questions.answer: In vitro, Li and colleagues 2017 showed that bacterial proteins shared with arsenic (AnoA, AioAB, ArsB, Acr3, GlpF) oxidize, efflux, or take up Sb(III). Deng and colleagues 2021, a review, state that the genes required for microbial antimony methylation are still unknown. Engrola and colleagues 2023 found antimonite in the arsenite-oxidase active site and state that Sb(III) is oxidized about 6,500 times more slowly than As(III). In mice, Wu and colleagues 2025 found gut and bile-acid changes after a high gavage dose of potassium antimony tartrate (10 mg/kg), which is not a consumer-product dose. In hospitalized infants, Yan and colleagues 2025 report a negative association between serum antimony and the Chao1 diversity index, without a single-metal beta in the main text. In saliva, Davis and colleagues 2021 associated antimony with oral taxa and decayed teeth. Zeldin and colleagues 2023 associated antimony air-release inventories with atopic dermatitis billing in one U.S. region and, in vitro, perturbed a skin commensal and a neuronal itch receptor. That is not a diaper-area cohort, and the printed billing code does not match the title.
